title: Rate and speed: d = s × t
subject: math

objectives.text: Read a speed as a rate: 60 km/h as 60 km covered in every hour
successCriteria: I can say that 60 km/h means 60 km covered in every hour
I can show the bus at 60 km after one hour, 120 km after two and 180 km after three
assessmentPoints: Rate answers in the opening activity
Responses when the speed-is-not-distance trap is sprung in the third activity

objectives.text: Find a distance by multiplying speed by time, and flip the formula to find a speed or a time
successCriteria: I can work out 60 × 2.5 = 150 km, checking it as 60 + 60 + 30
I can flip the formula to speed = distance ÷ time and time = distance ÷ speed
assessmentPoints: Distance answers in the second activity
Worksheet answers in the closing practice

activities.title: One hour at a time: read 60 km/h as a rate
Build the distance in parts, then multiply

differentiation.support: Provide a number line marked in 30 km half-hour steps so the half-hour distance can be read off before it is discussed.

activities.title: Land the formula family: multiply, then flip

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why half the time at the same speed gives half the distance.
